schema_note: Custom format, composed in this thread because the architect skill's canonical templates (questions/, knowledge/, templates/) weren't available in this session's environment. A fresh Claude Code session can read this file directly and move task by task respecting depends_on and status, with or without the /architect-next command.
ordering_rule: Don't start a phase without closing the previous one. Phase 1 exists to invalidate the project early if the camera plugin can't hit the necessary fidelity — see RUMBO.md, 'The technical risk that goes first'.

tasks.title: Capacitor project scaffold
tasks.description: React 19.2.8 + TypeScript + Vite 8.0.9 + Zustand 5.0.15, wrapped in Capacitor 8.5 (adopts UIScene). Add the iOS platform. Check the TypeScript version with `npm view typescript version` at install time — deliberately unpinned in this document, resolved in the moment.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN `npx cap open ios` is run and the app is built on a physical device THE SYSTEM SHALL show the app's blank screen with no native build errors.
tasks.verify_command: npm run build && npx cap sync ios
tasks.verify_note: The Xcode build itself is confirmed by opening the project and running on a device — there's no way to automate that part with a command that exits 0. Automated part (verify_command) passes as of 2026-08-16; opening in Xcode and running on hardware is still open, no device access from this environment.

tasks.title: Native camera plugin skeleton
tasks.description: Custom Capacitor plugin (Swift) that wraps AVFoundation directly — not `@capacitor/camera`. Just the capture session and one call that takes a photo without fine control yet; it's the scaffolding, not the full functionality.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the plugin method is called from JS THE SYSTEM SHALL return an image captured by AVFoundation, visible in the app.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification on a physical device — mandatory, the simulator has no real camera (see CLAUDE.md). Code written as of 2026-08-16 (CameraCapturePlugin.swift/.m + the JS wrapper and a manual test button in App.tsx) but not yet built or run on hardware — no Xcode/device access from this environment.

tasks.title: Lock exposure/focus/white balance across frames
tasks.description: The part that actually matters: manually expose the first capture and keep those values fixed (AVCaptureDevice.lockConfiguration, exposureMode/focusMode .locked) for the whole stop-motion session, instead of every photo re-exposing on its own.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN 10 consecutive frames are captured of a static scene under constant light THE SYSTEM SHALL produce 10 images with visually identical exposure and focus to each other — no flicker from auto re-exposure.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification: capture the sequence, play it back at 12fps, confirm by eye there's no flicker. This is the criterion that decides whether the project continues or gets rethought — see RUMBO.md. Code written as of 2026-08-16 (lockCaptureSettings/unlockCaptureSettings on CameraCapturePlugin, KVO-waits for isAdjustingExposure/isAdjustingFocus to settle before locking) plus lock/unlock buttons and a multi-frame filmstrip in the App.tsx test harness — but never compiled or run, no Xcode/device access from this environment. The actual 10-frames-no-flicker check hasn't happened.

phases.name: Local capture + drawing engine, no cloud

tasks.title: Port Trace's core/ pattern, adapted to camera cels
tasks.description: types.ts, math.ts, document.ts, history.ts — same layered design as Trace (no DOM, no React), but a Cel can now originate from a captured photo as well as a drawn stroke.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the engine test suite runs THE SYSTEM SHALL pass with no failures, including a test confirming a camera Cel and a drawn Cel share the same compositing interface.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-08-16 (82/82). Built ahead of 1.3's device verification on explicit owner instruction ("start what you can now, easiest to hardest") — this task doesn't touch native code or WebGL, so it isn't at risk from a camera-plugin rethink the way 2.2+ would be. Trimmed from Trace's document.ts on purpose, not by oversight: no rig/skeleton, sprite-swap, text layers, adjustment layers, layer masks, layer groups, or audio track — none are in Clumsyloop's v1 scope (see CLAUDE.md). LayerKind is 'camera' | 'draw' instead of Trace's 'draw' | 'reference' | 'adjustment' — that split is the actual product differentiator.

tasks.title: WebGL2 renderer: compositing camera frame + drawn layers
tasks.description: gl/renderer.ts — upload the captured photo as a texture, composite it with the drawing layers on top, all alpha-premultiplied. A single Y-flip pass, same as Trace.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a document with a camera Cel and a drawn Cel on top is rendered THE SYSTEM SHALL show both composited correctly, with no color halos or orientation mismatch.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-07. Visual verification done headlessly (Playwright + SwiftShader, this environment has no physical device either) via a new RendererHarness component (window.__clumsyloop) and scripts/renderer-smoke.mjs, reading back with renderer.toImageData() rather than a canvas screenshot — same preserveDrawingBuffer:false trap Trace's CLAUDE.md documents. Checks a four-quadrant synthetic photo (catches an orientation flip a solid color couldn't) with a real StrokeBuilder-generated pencil stroke composited on top: all four quadrants keep their own color, the stroke reads clearly darker than the photo under it, and the area just beside the stroke matches the plain photo color with no dark fringe. A screenshot for human eyeballing confirms the same by eye. Trimmed hard from Trace's renderer.ts, all flagged in gl/renderer.ts's own header comment: no GPU texture residency budget/eviction (a real concern for 'hundreds of photos' per RUMBO.md, deliberately deferred until the capture UI, task 2.3, produces real frame counts to profile against instead of guessing), no mesh skinning/rig, no adjustment layers, no selection, no pigment-mix wet blending (one ported brush.ts preset sets pigmentMix, but live stroke merging is the future drawing UI's job), no thumbnail downscaling (task 2.3 is the first actual caller). Kept in full: all 13 BlendModes and brush stamping (drawStamps), since types.ts/brush.ts already commit to them.

tasks.title: Capture UI: onion skin, shutter, filmstrip
tasks.description: Main capture screen — shutter button that calls the native plugin, onion-skin overlay of the previous frame, filmstrip thumbnail strip.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user taps the shutter THE SYSTEM SHALL add a new frame to the filmstrip and update the onion skin to show that frame as a reference for the next one.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification on device.

tasks.title: Local export to .mp4 with watermark on the free plan
tasks.description: Encode the full filmstrip (camera + composited drawing layers) to .mp4 via AVFoundation. Watermark gated on entitlement state — which doesn't exist yet at this phase, so for now the free plan is always assumed.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a project of at least 3 frames is exported THE SYSTEM SHALL produce a .mp4 file playable outside the app, with the watermark visible.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification: open the exported .mp4 in another app.

tasks.title: Local project persistence
tasks.description: Save/resume a project (frames + layers + metadata) on local disk, no network. A stop-motion project is hundreds of photos — specifically test that closing and reopening the app loses nothing.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the app is closed mid capture session and reopened THE SYSTEM SHALL restore the project exactly as it was, frame by frame.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-08. Built ahead of 2.3 (capture UI) on explicit owner instruction, same kind of exception as 2.1/2.2: persistence logic doesn't touch the camera plugin or need a real shutter button to exercise it, only a document with cels in it (synthetic ones here, same reasoning as the 2.2 harness). 2.4 (export) was intentionally NOT started alongside this — it needs native AVFoundation/Swift work that shares phase 1's device-verification limitation (can write the code, can't build or run it from this environment), whereas 2.5 is fully browser/IndexedDB-based and testable here. IndexedDB chosen over Capacitor's Filesystem plugin (the owner's call) to avoid a new native dependency for v1; flagged as a real device-reliability question worth another look once actual on-device behavior can be observed. PNG encode/decode uses upng-js (already the library RUMBO.md's known-debts note pointed at) instead of Trace's canvas.toBlob() specifically so core/io.ts runs under npm test (no DOM/canvas in Node) — found and worked around a real decode bug in upng-js@2.1.0 along the way (auto-selected palette mode crashes toRGBA8; forced off via encode's undocumented 6th argument, forbidPlte). Split three ways per CLAUDE.md's gl/-is-the-only-WebGL-contact rule: core/io.ts (pure metadata + PNG, unit tested, 9 new tests in io.test.ts), gl/projectIO.ts (Surface <-> pixels glue), state/projectStore.ts (IndexedDB, degrades to a no-op under Node same as palettes.ts does for localStorage). Verified in a real browser via scripts/persistence-smoke.mjs (Playwright): save a synthetic two-cel-camera-layer + one-draw-layer project, reload the page (the closest proxy this environment has for force-quit + relaunch — no physical device), confirm every field and every composited pixel survives. Along the way this also caught and fixed a real aliasing bug in Renderer.renderDocumentFrame (task 2.2): its returned surface is a reused scratch buffer, so holding two frames' results at once silently corrupts the first — now documented on the method itself, not just fixed locally.

tasks.title: Drawing UI: canvas, pointer input, brush/color panels
tasks.description: Connect the already-ported brush.ts and the curated palettes to a real interactive canvas — pointer events (mouse/pen/touch) drive StrokeBuilder, stamps paint onto the active layer's cel via drawStamps, the result composites and presents live. Not originally itemized in this document (added retroactively on 2026-09-09): checkpoint.md's 2026-08-16 entry already flagged brush.ts as groundwork ported with no consumer yet, and this is that consumer. Single fixed draw layer, single frame — no timeline, no camera layer (that's 2.3, still blocked on device verification).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user drags a pointer across the canvas THE SYSTEM SHALL paint a visible stroke with the selected brush and color, and THE SYSTEM SHALL let the user switch brush or color between strokes without affecting ink already on the canvas.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-09. Owner asked what else could be added while phase 1 stays blocked; this was picked over two other camera-independent options (Firestore rules, the web half of export) as the highest-value one — the actual product differentiator, not backend plumbing. New gl/engine.ts is deliberately minimal, not a port of Trace's core/engine.ts: no revision/touch()/subscribe pub-sub (CLAUDE.md's documented pattern) yet, since the canvas is the only consumer so far and updates itself imperatively after every mutation — add the pub-sub once a second UI piece (layers panel, frame counter) actually needs to react to engine state, not before. No wet-stroke staging surface either (stamps go straight onto the permanent cel); no pigment-mix blending for the one brush.ts preset that wants it (Watercolor); no undo — all real, deliberate simplifications for this first slice, not oversights. Added erase-mode support to Renderer.drawStamps (blendFunc(ZERO, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) instead of the normal src-over) since brush.ts's two eraser presets need it and nothing had exercised that path yet. New state/tool.ts (active brush id + color, Zustand) split out the same way palettes.ts already is. Verified with real pointer events (not synthetic Stamp arrays) via scripts/drawing-smoke.mjs (Playwright): draws an actual stroke, confirms it's dark ink not blank paper; switches color and draws again, confirms the new stroke is the new color AND the earlier stroke is byte-for-byte unaffected; switches to the eraser brush and confirms it removes ink; confirms Clear resets the layer. All three Playwright smoke tests (renderer/persistence/drawing) still pass together — no regressions.

tasks.title: Firebase project + Sign in with Apple
tasks.description: Create the Firebase project, Firebase Auth with Sign in with Apple as the primary method (capacitor-firebase, current verified plugins: messaging 8.3.0, analytics 8.3.0, firestore 8.1.0 — confirm the current version at install time).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user taps 'Sign in with Apple' THE SYSTEM SHALL create or recover their account and leave them authenticated in Firebase Auth.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification on device — Sign in with Apple doesn't work in every simulator environment.

tasks.title: Firestore schema: users, projects, entitlements
tasks.description: Base collections and security rules — each user can only read/write their own projects and their own entitlement, never another user's.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN an authenticated user tries to read another user's entitlement document THE SYSTEM SHALL deny access via Firestore rules.
tasks.verify_note: Requires the rules tests to already be written against the Firestore emulator before this command means anything.

tasks.title: StoreKit 2 purchase flow (client)
tasks.description: Subscription screen, native StoreKit 2 integration (or equivalent Capacitor plugin) to start the purchase and receive the transaction.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user completes a sandbox purchase THE SYSTEM SHALL receive the client-side transaction signed by StoreKit.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification with an App Store Connect sandbox account.

tasks.title: Cloud Function: receipt validation → entitlement in Firestore
tasks.description: The client transaction is never trusted alone — the Cloud Function validates against the App Store Server API and only then writes the entitlement.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a valid sandbox transaction is sent to the Cloud Function THE SYSTEM SHALL write the entitlement to Firestore; WHEN a tampered or fake transaction is sent THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it without writing anything.

tasks.title: Gate premium features behind the entitlement
tasks.description: Remove the watermark, enable extra layers and cloud save only if the Firestore entitlement is active.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user's entitlement is active THE SYSTEM SHALL export with no watermark; WHEN it isn't THE SYSTEM SHALL keep it.

tasks.title: clips collection in Firestore + Storage upload
tasks.description: Publishing pipeline: upload the exported .mp4 to Firebase Storage, create the `clips` document with the URL and metadata (author, date, no likes/comments fields — not part of v1 scope).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user publishes a clip THE SYSTEM SHALL create a `clips` document whose video URL is publicly accessible.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification — confirm the resulting URL plays back in a separate browser.

tasks.title: Feed UI: chronological list, playback
tasks.description: No ranking, no algorithm — simple chronological order, as decided in RUMBO.md.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the feed is opened THE SYSTEM SHALL show published clips ordered newest to oldest, playable inline.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification on device.

tasks.title: Publish flow from the export screen
tasks.description: 'Publish' button next to export, which triggers 4.1 without the user having to leave the export flow.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user exports and taps 'Publish' THE SYSTEM SHALL complete the upload and show the clip in the feed with no extra steps.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification.

tasks.title: Native share sheet to external networks
tasks.description: UIActivityViewController (via Capacitor's Share plugin) with the .mp4 and a prefilled caption including the app's hashtag, targeting Instagram/TikTok/X/Threads/Facebook — no per-platform API integration.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user taps 'Share' THE SYSTEM SHALL open the native iOS share sheet with the video attached and the hashtag already written in the text.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification on device.

tasks.title: Report button + reports collection
tasks.description: Any clip in the feed can be reported. The report stores who, which clip, and a reason.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a user reports a clip THE SYSTEM SHALL create a `reports` document referencing that clip.

tasks.title: Cloud Function: report → hide clip from feed
tasks.description: Once a report threshold is crossed (to be defined, start conservative — 1 report is enough to hide while under review, not to delete), the clip stops appearing in feed queries without being deleted yet.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a clip reaches the report threshold THE SYSTEM SHALL exclude it from the query that feeds the public feed.

tasks.title: Minimal internal review panel
tasks.description: Simple web page, protected by Firebase Auth with an admin allowlist, to view reported clips and decide: restore or permanently delete. Not a product — the minimum needed to meet Apple's requirement of acting within 24 hours.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN an admin deletes a reported clip from the panel THE SYSTEM SHALL remove it from Firestore and Storage, not just hide it.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification.

phases.name: Packaging and submission for Apple review

tasks.title: App Store Connect listing
tasks.description: Screenshots, description, privacy labels (Apple requires declaring what data is collected — camera, photos, user content via Firebase) consistent with what the app actually does.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the App Store Connect privacy form is completed THE SYSTEM SHALL declare every type of data the app actually collects, with no omissions.
tasks.verify_note: Manual review against the code: camera, photos, user identifier, generated content.

tasks.title: UGC guideline compliance checklist
tasks.description: Explicitly confirm, before submitting, that report + block + takedown within 24h (phase 5) are complete and documented — the most common rejection reason for apps with a feed.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN Apple's guideline 1.2 (UGC) checklist is reviewed THE SYSTEM SHALL have evidence for every point (working report, working block, documented takedown process).
tasks.verify_note: Manual review against Apple's current guideline at submission time — it may have changed since this document was written.

tasks.title: TestFlight build
tasks.description: First signed build uploaded to TestFlight, tested by at least one person outside the development before submitting for public review.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the TestFlight build is installed on a device other than the development one THE SYSTEM SHALL run without crashing through the full flow: capture, draw, export, publish.
tasks.verify_note: Manual verification, external device.

tasks.title: Submit for review
tasks.description: Formal submission to Apple. This is the last step of the bundle — what happens after (rejections, iteration) isn't in this document because it depends on Apple's actual response.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the build is submitted for review THE SYSTEM SHALL be in 'Waiting for Review' state in App Store Connect.
tasks.verify_note: Manual confirmation in App Store Connect.
